newsitem.title: UK: UK unveils user-friendly Crown copyright licence.
newsitem.headline: UK unveils user-friendly Crown copyright licence.

text.p: The government on Tuesday unveiled new simplified Crown copyright licensing arrangements that it said would make it easier for electronic publishers to include official material in their information services.

Holders of the new licence, which is renewable after seven years, would be able to reproduce material without seeking prior permission from the Crown and at a standardised royalty rate, public services minister Roger Freeman said.
He said in a written parliamentary answer the licence would offer great benefits to the electronic publishing industry, in particular the legal publishing sector.
"It will help create a climate conducive to the growth of commercial electronic information services, both on open and closed networks," Freeman said.

The new licence, called QLM/3, will be offered to publishers on a non-exclusive basis from November 1 and covers quasi-legislative material such as codes of practice and official guidance on how statutes are to be interpreted.
